Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 108, verse 1:

﴿Indeed, We have granted you﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿al-Kawthar﴾. It is a river in Paradise, which is his basin (ḥawḍ) to which his community will come. And al-Kawthar: abundant good, including prophethood, the Qur'an, intercession, and the like.
﴿So pray to your Lord﴾: the prayer of ʿId al-Naḥr (the Feast of Sacrifice), ﴿and sacrifice﴾: your sacrifice (nusuk).

Verse 3: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off [from all good], or the one without offspring.﴾ "Your enemy" means the one who hates you, and "the one cut off" (al-abtar) means the one severed from every good, or the one without a posterity. It was revealed concerning al-'As ibn Wa'il, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) was called "abtar" (cut off) when his son al-Qasim died.
